$comment: Where the mobile halves depart from Kasane. Kurobeni keeps the same file for the web. A part that is not listed here has to match its .kb-* rule.

deviations.what: The space ladder is the compact remap: 16 is 12, 24 is 16, 32 is 24, 48 is 32, 64 is 48 and 96 is 64. The unremapped ladder is exported as room.
deviations.why: The web turns data-kb-density=compact on itself under 768, and a phone is never the other case. Controls are untouched, which is the rule the web keeps too.

deviations.what: The type ladder is emitted as unscaled numbers instead of final sizes.
deviations.why: Both platforms let the reader set a text scale, and a size the app fixes ignores it. Expo multiplies by the font scale, SwiftUI names the step to scale against.

deviations.what: A shadow is emitted as x, y, blur, colour and opacity instead of one box-shadow string.
deviations.why: Neither platform parses CSS. The values are the same ones.

deviations.what: The safe area is not a token.
deviations.why: It has no web equivalent and it is not a constant: the OS reports it, and it changes with the device and the orientation.

deviations.what: The bar sits 16 below the safe area rather than 16 below the top of the viewport, and spans the width less 16 each side instead of fitting its content.
deviations.why: A phone has a status bar and a notch in the 16 the web can spend, and a brand with a back control and an action fills the width anyway.

deviations.what: Every :hover rule is dropped; the :active rule is what a press shows.
deviations.why: There is no pointer to hover with. A finger arrives already pressing.

deviations.what: There is no refresh control and no pull to refresh.
deviations.why: The web has neither. A query refetches when a screen mounts and when the connection returns, which is what a page load does on the web.
This is the compact remap the web already applies to .kb-head__title under 768.
